# [Test] [NPU] rl: Add sleep/wake scheduler unit and 1-NPU smoke tests

Per the RL Test Consolidation RFC (#47624), this PR lands the first feature area (sleep/wake) of the NPU-side test consolidation: file ownership, coverage docstrings, and CI integration for Ascend.

**Precision scope: BF16 only.** Per the RFC's BF16 precision target, all cases in this PR plan and assert BF16 only (other dtypes — FP16/FP32/INT8/W8A8 — are explicitly out of scope for this round). The 1-NPU smoke launches the server with an explicit `--dtype bfloat16` (never dtype-inferred) and asserts the effective dtype via `/server_info` (`dtype == "bfloat16"` + the flag pinned in `launch_command`) before any scenario assertion, so all bitwise determinism anchors validate the BF16 numerics path specifically. The unit tier is dtype-agnostic (mocked devices) and inherits the contract from its smoke sibling.

## What's here

**1. `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_memory_release.py`** (new, CPU tier)

Pins the `release_memory_occupation` / `resume_memory_occupation` state-machine contracts (`SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager`):

- release asserts a fully idle engine; an `engine_paused` release passes with `ignore_waiting=True`
- default tags pause all memory types in the fixed order `kv_cache -> weights -> cuda_graph`; the request-side tag order is normalized
- the device is synchronized during release (a strict synchronize-BEFORE-first-pause ordering assertion is included commented-out, to be enabled together with the pending Ascend SDMA-race fix)
- `kv_cache` release flushes the cache exactly once; weights release does not
- release is idempotent; unknown tags are silently tracked today (pinned deliberately — the RFC proposes strict rejection)
- resume is not idempotent: unknown tag raises `KeyError`; weights resume without the release-time stash raises `AttributeError`; the happy path imports the stash and clears it

**2. `test/registered/npu/rl/test_npu_release_resume_memory.py`** (new, 1-NPU tier)

- **S0 BF16 precision contract**: both instances launch with `--dtype bfloat16`; `/server_info` must echo `dtype == "bfloat16"` with the flag pinned in `launch_command` (weights + KV cache follow the model dtype on the ascend attention backend)
- KV-only sleep roundtrip keeps greedy outputs bit-identical (under BF16)
- full cycle with device-memory evidence logging (on current CANN/TMS the TMS pause does not return pages to the device-level pool, so the watermark is informational, not an assertion) + the RL standard chain `release(all) -> resume(all) -> update_weights_from_disk -> /health_generate`
- level-1 equivalence: with `--enable-weights-cpu-backup`, `release(all) -> resume(all)` without any update restores outputs bitwise (regression probe for the sleep-pollution class of bugs)
- `cuda_graph` tag contract: accepted, documented as a release no-op on NPU today

Both files carry coverage docstrings (behaviors, APIs, NPU-specific risks, sibling CUDA tests) per the RFC.

## CI registration

- unit file: `register_cpu_ci(est_time=8, suite="base-a-test-cpu")`
- NPU file: `register_npu_ci(est_time=1800, suite="nightly-npu-a3-merged", nightly=True)`

## Validation

Validated on Ascend 910 (openEuler 22.03, CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10 + torch_npu, Qwen3-0.6B, TP=1, `--dtype bfloat16`):
- unit: 11 passed
- 1-NPU smoke: 2 passed (BF16 contract asserted on both instances; KV-only roundtrip clean; level-1 cpu-backup restore bitwise-identical; full RL chain serves after update)

Environment knobs: `RL_FEAT_MODEL_PATH` (model override, defaults to `LLAMA_3_2_1B_INSTRUCT_WEIGHTS_PATH`) and `RL_FEAT_NPU_ID` (die selection, default "0").

Related: #47624 (tracks the remaining feature areas: pause/resume, weight update + metrics, weight checker, routed experts, response schema, CPU lifecycle-state, weight telemetry)

@@ -0,0 +1,239 @@
+"""1-NPU smoke tests for the sleep/wake (release/resume) lifecycle.
+
+RL Test Consolidation (sgl-project/sglang#47624) — sleep/wake area, 1-NPU tier.
+File ownership per RFC section 5 (sleep/wake, 1-NPU smoke).
+
+BF16 precision contract (RFC section 4): the RL rollout engine on Ascend runs
+BF16 weights and KV cache. Both instances below launch with an explicit
+``--dtype bfloat16`` (never dtype-inferred) and assert the effective dtype via
+``/server_info`` (``dtype == "bfloat16"`` and ``launch_command`` pins the flag)
+before any scenario assertion runs — S0. All bitwise determinism anchors
+(S1/S3) therefore validate the BF16 numerics path specifically.
+
+Coverage (scenarios map to the npu188 experiment matrix):
+- S0  BF16 precision contract: server runs with explicit --dtype bfloat16
+      and /server_info echoes the effective dtype (weights + KV cache follow
+      the model dtype on the ascend attention backend).
+- S1  KV-only sleep roundtrip is clean: release(kv_cache) -> resume(kv_cache)
+      keeps greedy outputs bitwise identical (E5 template).
+- S2  Full cycle with the RL standard chain: release(all) / resume(all)
+      lifecycle (device-memory deltas logged as evidence — on this CANN/TMS
+      stack TMS pause does not return pages to the device pool, so the
+      watermark is informational only), then
+      update_weights_from_disk(same weights) + /health_generate succeed.
+      NOTE: under default (level-2 equivalent) semantics the phase between
+      resume and update deliberately has NO output-correctness assertion —
+      non-buffer runtime tensors are dropped by sleep (known defect, tracked
+      separately as a defect-fix PR; see sleep-mode consolidation report).
+- S4  cuda_graph tag contract: release(["cuda_graph"]) is accepted (HTTP 200).
+      On NPU this tag currently has no actual release effect (TMS NPU has no
+      cuda-graph context) — memory assertions therefore only cover
+      weights+kv_cache.
+- S3  Level-1 equivalence on a --enable-weights-cpu-backup server:
+      release(all) -> resume(all) WITHOUT any update keeps outputs bitwise
+      identical (E1-B template). This is the regression probe for the sleep
+      pollution defect: any content drift here is a real regression.
+
+Instance strategy: one shared server instance A (default config) runs S4, S1,
+S2 in sequence; instance B (--enable-weights-cpu-backup) runs S3 alone.
+
+Server die selection: set RL_FEAT_NPU_ID (default "0") to pin
+ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES for the launched server.
+
+Sibling CUDA test:
+  test/registered/rl/test_multi_instance_release_memory_occupation.py
+"""
+
+import os
+import unittest
+
+import requests
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_npu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import (
+    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+    CustomTestCase,
+    find_available_port,
+    popen_launch_server,
+)
+
+try:
+    import torch
+    import torch_npu  # noqa: F401
+
+    _NPU_AVAILABLE = torch.npu.is_available()
+except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - non-NPU environments
+    _NPU_AVAILABLE = False
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import kill_process_tree
+from sglang.test.ascend.test_ascend_utils import LLAMA_3_2_1B_INSTRUCT_WEIGHTS_PATH
+
+register_npu_ci(est_time=1800, suite="nightly-npu-a3-merged", nightly=True)
+
+# Model override for hosts without the default weights cached (e.g. npu188
+# only caches Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B): export RL_FEAT_MODEL_PATH=<absolute path>.
+MODEL = os.environ.get("RL_FEAT_MODEL_PATH", LLAMA_3_2_1B_INSTRUCT_WEIGHTS_PATH)
+
+PROMPTS = [
+    "The capital of France is",
+    "Write a one-sentence summary of photosynthesis.",
+    "1 2 3 4 5",
+    "你好，请用一句话介绍自己。",
+    "def add(a, b):",
+]
+
+
+def _npu_used_memory_mb() -> float:
+    free, total = torch.npu.mem_get_info()
+    return (total - free) / (1024**2)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_NPU_AVAILABLE, "Requires an Ascend NPU device")
+class TestNpuReleaseResumeMemory(CustomTestCase):
+    def _launch(self, extra_args):
+        port = find_available_port(31000)
+        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
+        env = dict(os.environ)
+        env["ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = os.environ.get("RL_FEAT_NPU_ID", "0")
+        return popen_launch_server(
+            MODEL,
+            self.base_url,
+            timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+            other_args=["--attention-backend", "ascend", "--dtype", "bfloat16"]
+            + extra_args,
+            env=env,
+        )
+
+    def _assert_bf16_contract(self):
+        """S0: the running server must be pinned to BF16 (RFC section 4).
+        Asserted against /server_info — the resolution result (``dtype``) and
+        the actually-issued ``launch_command`` — so an accidental dtype
+        inference change fails here instead of silently redefining the
+        scenarios' numerics."""
+        info = requests.get(self.base_url + "/server_info", timeout=120).json()
+        self.assertEqual(
+            str(info.get("dtype", "")).lower(),
+            "bfloat16",
+            f"server must run BF16 weights/KV, got dtype={info.get('dtype')!r}",
+        )
+        launch = info.get("launch_command", "")
+        self.assertIn(
+            "bfloat16",
+            str(launch).lower(),
+            f"launch command must pin --dtype bfloat16: {launch}",
+        )
+
+    def _post(self, path, payload):
+        r = requests.post(
+            self.base_url + path,
+            json=payload,
+            timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(r.status_code, 200, f"{path} -> {r.status_code}: {r.text}")
+        return r
+
+    def _generate_all(self, max_new_tokens=64):
+        return [
+            requests.post(
+                self.base_url + "/generate",
+                json={
+                    "text": p,
+                    "sampling_params": {
+                        "temperature": 0,
+                        "max_new_tokens": max_new_tokens,
+                        "ignore_eos": True,
+                    },
+                },
+                timeout=300,
+            ).json()["text"]
+            for p in PROMPTS
+        ]
+
+    def test_instance_a_lifecycle_memory_and_update_chain(self):
+        """Shared default-config instance: S4 (cuda_graph tag), S1 (KV-only
+        roundtrip), S2 (memory watermark + RL chain)."""
+        process = self._launch(["--enable-memory-saver"])
+        try:
+            # S0: BF16 precision contract for this instance.
+            self._assert_bf16_contract()
+
+            # S4: cuda_graph tag is accepted; on NPU it is a release no-op today.
+            self._post("/release_memory_occupation", {"tags": ["cuda_graph"]})
+            self._post("/resume_memory_occupation", {"tags": ["cuda_graph"]})
+
+            # S1: KV-only sleep roundtrip must be content-clean.
+            self._post("/release_memory_occupation", {"tags": ["kv_cache"]})
+            self._post("/resume_memory_occupation", {"tags": ["kv_cache"]})
+            baseline = self._generate_all()
+            self._post("/release_memory_occupation", {"tags": ["kv_cache"]})
+            self._post("/resume_memory_occupation", {"tags": ["kv_cache"]})
+            after_kv = self._generate_all()
+            self.assertEqual(
+                after_kv, baseline, "KV-only sleep roundtrip must be deterministic"
+            )
+
+            # S2: full cycle with the RL chain. No output assertion between
+            # resume(all) and the weight update: default (level-2 equivalent)
+            # semantics leave non-buffer runtime tensors undefined after sleep
+            # (known defect, separate fix PR).
+            #
+            # Memory evidence: on this CANN/TMS stack pausing a TMS region does
+            # NOT return pages to the device-level free pool (observed delta
+            # ~2 MB), so torch.npu.mem_get_info is NOT a valid release oracle
+            # here. We log the deltas as evidence and keep lifecycle + content
+            # assertions as the hard contract; device-level memory evidence
+            # needs npu-smi sampling or TMS-internal accounting instead.
+            used_before = _npu_used_memory_mb()
+            self._post("/release_memory_occupation", {})
+            used_released = _npu_used_memory_mb()
+            print(
+                f"[memory-evidence] release(all) device delta = "
+                f"{used_before - used_released:.0f} MB"
+            )
+            self.assertGreaterEqual(used_before - used_released, 0.0)
+
+            self._post("/resume_memory_occupation", {})
+            used_resumed = _npu_used_memory_mb()
+            print(
+                f"[memory-evidence] resume(all) device delta = "
+                f"{used_resumed - used_released:.0f} MB"
+            )
+
+            r = self._post(
+                "/update_weights_from_disk", {"model_path": MODEL, "flush_cache": True}
+            )
+            self.assertTrue(
+                r.json().get("success"),
+                f"update_weights_from_disk failed: {r.text}",
+            )
+            health = requests.get(self.base_url + "/health_generate", timeout=300)
+            self.assertEqual(health.status_code, 200)
+        finally:
+            kill_process_tree(process.pid)
+
+    def test_instance_b_level1_bitwise_restore_with_cpu_backup(self):
+        """--enable-weights-cpu-backup (level-1 equivalent): sleep->resume
+        without any weight update must restore outputs bitwise (E1-B). Any
+        drift here is the sleep pollution defect regressing."""
+        process = self._launch(["--enable-memory-saver", "--enable-weights-cpu-backup"])
+        try:
+            # S0: BF16 precision contract for this instance.
+            self._assert_bf16_contract()
+
+            baseline = self._generate_all()
+
+            self._post("/release_memory_occupation", {})
+            self._post("/resume_memory_occupation", {})
+
+            restored = self._generate_all()
+            self.assertEqual(
+                restored,
+                baseline,
+                "level-1 (cpu backup) sleep must restore outputs bitwise",
+            )
+        finally:
+            kill_process_tree(process.pid)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

@@ -0,0 +1,256 @@
+"""Unit tests for the release/resume memory-occupation state machine.
+
+RL Test Consolidation (sgl-project/sglang#47624) — sleep/wake area, CPU tier.
+File ownership per RFC section 5 (sleep/wake, CPU/unit).
+
+Coverage:
+- release asserts a fully idle engine; an engine_paused release passes with
+  ignore_waiting=True.
+- Default tags pause all memory types in the fixed order kv -> weights ->
+  cuda_graph; the request-side tag order is normalized.
+- The device is synchronized during release. NOTE: on main the synchronize
+  currently runs AFTER the pool pauses — the Ascend SDMA-race fix (synchronize
+  BEFORE the first pause) is pending as a separate defect-fix PR; a strict
+  ordering assertion is kept (commented) in
+  test_release_synchronizes_device_during_release and must be enabled when
+  that fix lands.
+- kv_cache release flushes the cache exactly once; weights release does not.
+- release is idempotent (offload_tags is a set); unknown tags are silently
+  tracked today — the RFC proposes strict rejection, so this test pins the
+  current behavior to make any future tightening a deliberate change.
+- resume is NOT idempotent: an unknown tag raises KeyError; a weights resume
+  without the release-time static-state stash raises AttributeError.
+- a proper weights resume imports the stashed static state and clears it.
+
+NPU risk probed (indirectly, via call ordering): the synchronize/pause race
+that aborts Ascend devices with SDMA channel errors.
+
+BF16 precision scope (RFC section 4): this unit tier exercises the
+release/resume state machine against mocked devices and is deliberately
+dtype-agnostic; the BF16 contract (explicit --dtype bfloat16 + /server_info
+dtype assertion) is enforced by the 1-NPU smoke sibling
+test/registered/npu/rl/test_npu_release_resume_memory.py (S0).
+
+Sibling CUDA test:
+  test/registered/rl/test_multi_instance_release_memory_occupation.py
+Empirical background: npu188 TMS probes (region content zeroing, SDMA error
+without prior synchronize) — see sleep-mode consolidation report.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.constants import (
+    GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH,
+    GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE,
+    GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS,
+)
+from sglang.srt.disaggregation.mode import DisaggregationMode
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import (
+    ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+    ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput,
+)
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.weight_updater import (
+    SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager,
+)
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=8, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+WU_MODULE = "sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.weight_updater"
+
+
+class TestSchedulerMemoryRelease(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.updater = SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager.__new__(
+            SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager
+        )
+        self.updater.scheduler = MagicMock()
+        self.updater.scheduler._engine_paused = False
+        self.updater.scheduler.disaggregation_mode = DisaggregationMode.NULL
+        self.updater.is_fully_idle = lambda **kwargs: True
+        self.updater.offload_tags = set()
+        self.updater.memory_saver_adapter = MagicMock()
+        self.updater.tp_worker = MagicMock()
+        self.updater.tp_cpu_group = None
+        self.updater.flush_cache = MagicMock()
+        # _assert_weight_cache_inactive is a class method (slots dataclass):
+        # patch it at class level instead of assigning an instance attribute.
+        patcher_wci = patch.object(
+            SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager, "_assert_weight_cache_inactive"
+        )
+        self.mock_wci = patcher_wci.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher_wci.stop)
+        # Shared ledger for device-sync and pool-pause call ordering.
+        self.events = []
+
+        patcher_barrier = patch("torch.distributed.barrier")
+        patcher_device = patch("torch.get_device_module")
+        patcher_export = patch(
+            f"{WU_MODULE}._export_static_state", return_value="STASH"
+        )
+        patcher_import = patch(f"{WU_MODULE}._import_static_state")
+        self.mock_barrier = patcher_barrier.start()
+        self.mock_device_module = patcher_device.start()
+        self.mock_export = patcher_export.start()
+        self.mock_import = patcher_import.start()
+        self.mock_device_module.return_value.synchronize.side_effect = lambda: (
+            self.events.append("sync")
+        )
+        self.updater.memory_saver_adapter.pause.side_effect = lambda tag: (
+            self.events.append(f"pause:{tag}")
+        )
+        self.addCleanup(patcher_barrier.stop)
+        self.addCleanup(patcher_device.stop)
+        self.addCleanup(patcher_export.stop)
+        self.addCleanup(patcher_import.stop)
+
+    def _release(self, tags=None):
+        return self.updater.release_memory_occupation(
+            ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=tags)
+        )
+
+    def _resume(self, tags=None):
+        return self.updater.resume_memory_occupation(
+            ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=tags)
+        )
+
+    def _pause_calls(self):
+        return [e for e in self.events if e.startswith("pause:")]
+
+    # --- idle prerequisite -------------------------------------------------
+
+    def test_release_rejected_while_requests_in_flight(self):
+        """release with an unfinished engine must assert before touching pools."""
+        self.updater.is_fully_idle = lambda **kwargs: False
+
+        with self.assertRaises(AssertionError):
+            self._release(tags=["kv_cache"])
+
+        self.updater.memory_saver_adapter.pause.assert_not_called()
+        self.assertEqual(self._pause_calls(), [])
+
+    def test_release_while_engine_paused_passes_ignore_waiting(self):
+        """A paused engine holds queued requests: release must consult
+        is_fully_idle with ignore_waiting=True instead of failing."""
+        seen = {}
+        self.updater.is_fully_idle = lambda **kwargs: seen.update(kwargs) or True
+        self.updater.scheduler._engine_paused = True
+
+        self._release(tags=["kv_cache"])
+
+        self.assertEqual(seen, {"ignore_waiting": True})
+
+    # --- execution order contracts ----------------------------------------
+
+    def test_release_default_tags_pause_all_types_in_fixed_order(self):
+        """tags=None must pause kv, weights, cuda_graph — in that order."""
+        self._release(tags=None)
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._pause_calls(),
+            [
+                f"pause:{GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE}",
+                f"pause:{GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS}",
+                f"pause:{GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH}",
+            ],
+        )
+
+    def test_release_request_tag_order_is_normalized(self):
+        """The caller's tag order must not change execution order: kv still
+        pauses before weights (single-request normalization contract)."""
+        self._release(tags=["weights", "kv_cache"])
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._pause_calls(),
+            [
+                f"pause:{GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE}",
+                f"pause:{GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS}",
+            ],
+        )
+
+    def test_release_synchronizes_device_during_release(self):
+        """release must synchronize the device at least once.
+
+        On main the synchronize currently runs AFTER the pool pauses. The
+        Ascend SDMA-race fix (synchronize BEFORE the first pause and after the
+        static-state export) is pending as a separate defect-fix PR; enable
+        the strict ordering below together with that fix:
+        """
+        self._release(tags=None)
+
+        self.assertIn("sync", self.events)
+
+        # Strict ordering (enable once the SDMA sync-before-pause fix lands):
+        # first_pause = next(
+        #     i for i, e in enumerate(self.events) if e.startswith("pause:")
+        # )
+        # self.assertLess(self.events.index("sync"), first_pause)
+
+    def test_release_kv_cache_flushes_exactly_once(self):
+        """kv_cache release flushes the cache once; weights release must not."""
+        self._release(tags=["kv_cache"])
+        self.assertEqual(self.updater.flush_cache.call_count, 1)
+
+        self.updater.flush_cache.reset_mock()
+        self._release(tags=["weights"])
+        self.updater.flush_cache.assert_not_called()
+
+    # --- idempotency and tag contracts -------------------------------------
+
+    def test_double_release_is_idempotent(self):
+        """Re-releasing the same tags must not raise nor duplicate state."""
+        self._release(tags=["weights"])
+        self._release(tags=["weights"])
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.updater.offload_tags, {GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS})
+        self.assertEqual(len(self._pause_calls()), 2)
+
+    def test_release_unknown_tag_is_silently_tracked(self):
+        """Current contract: unknown tags are added to offload_tags without
+        validation and never reach any pool pause. The consolidation RFC
+        proposes rejecting them; this test pins today's behavior so a future
+        strict-validation change updates this test deliberately."""
+        self._release(tags=["weights", "bogus-tag"])
+
+        self.assertIn("bogus-tag", self.updater.offload_tags)
+        self.assertEqual(self._pause_calls(), [f"pause:{GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS}"])
+
+    def test_resume_unknown_tag_raises_keyerror(self):
+        """resume removes tags from offload_tags: resuming a tag that was never
+        released must raise KeyError (resume is not idempotent today)."""
+        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+            self._resume(tags=["kv_cache"])
+
+    def test_resume_weights_without_prior_release_raises_attribute_error(self):
+        """A weights resume requires the static-state stash exported at release
+        time. With the tag manually present but no stash, resume must fail
+        loudly (AttributeError) rather than resume into undefined state."""
+        self.updater.offload_tags = {
+            GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE,
+            GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS,
+        }
+
+        with self.assertRaises(AttributeError):
+            self._resume(tags=["weights"])
+
+    def test_resume_weights_imports_stash_and_clears_it(self):
+        """The happy path: weights resume restores the exported static state
+        and drops the stash reference."""
+        self._release(tags=["weights"])
+        self.assertEqual(self.updater.stashed_model_static_state, "STASH")
+
+        self._resume(tags=["weights"])
+
+        self.mock_import.assert_called_once_with(
+            self.updater.tp_worker.model_runner.model, "STASH"
+        )
+        self.assertFalse(hasattr(self.updater, "stashed_model_static_state"))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
